Lets EQO find files such as PDFs and photos on your phone and attach them to a WhatsApp, email or text message you approve. EQO shows you the file names before anything is sent, and never reads app data or settings. Tap to open Android\'s page, switch it on for EQO, then come back.
On. EQO can find and attach files named in a task you approve. You can switch it off any time in Android Settings.
This phone has no All files access page. Look for it under Settings, Apps, Special app access.

Paste your OpenRouter API key and a model name from your account, then tap Check and save key. Your key stays encrypted on this phone and is never logged. OpenRouter may charge your account for usage.
Model name from OpenRouter (for example, provider/model)
Checking the key with the provider\u2026
Ready — your key is saved securely. Next: return to setup.
Needs attention — checking or saving the key failed. Follow the guidance below.
EQO needs Accessibility to read and tap the screen for tasks you choose. Next: open Android Accessibility settings, find EQO under Downloaded apps and turn it on. Only you can change this setting.
I turned it on — check again
Ready — screen control is on. Next: return to setup.
The EQO accessibility service is off. Open Settings > Accessibility > EQO and turn it on.
Android 13+ may block this grant for sideloaded apps. This is Android\'s protection, not an EQO error: Settings > Apps > EQO > three-dot menu > Allow restricted settings, then try the toggle again.

1. Connect this phone to Wi-Fi. Tap Find ports to enable the code notification.
2. Open Developer options, turn on Wireless debugging, then tap Pair device with pairing code.
3. Keep that dialog open. Reply to the EQO notification with the six-digit code. If ports are not found, type code and pairing port, optionally followed by the connection port, separated by spaces or commas. With no connection port yet, EQO waits up to one minute before pairing.
4. Return to EQO, tap Connect again, then tap Allow in EQO's helper prompt.
The code box here accepts the same format. Supplying both ports does not need discovery.
Code, optionally pairing port and connection port
Not paired. Open Android\'s pairing dialog and enter its six-digit code.
Paired, but not connected right now. Turn on Wireless debugging, then tap Connect again.
Needs re-pair. This phone no longer matches the pairing EQO recorded. Open Wireless debugging, tap Pair device with pairing code, and pair again.
Working… keep the pairing dialog open.
Enter a six-digit code, optionally followed by the pairing port and connection port, separated by spaces or commas. Ports must be 1024–65535 and different.
Wi-Fi needed. Connect this phone to Wi-Fi before pairing. On Android 11–12, turn off a VPN while finding ports.
Port search stopped. Tap Find ports to start it again. Each search lasts five minutes.
Looking for this phone\'s wireless debugging ports… Open the pairing dialog.
Both ports found. Only the six-digit code is needed.
Wireless debugging may be off, or its ports could not be found. Open Developer options and turn it on. If it is already on, use the port boxes below.
Ports not found yet. Keep the pairing dialog open, or enter its pairing port and the connection port from Wireless debugging.
Could not open Developer options. Open it from your phone\'s Settings.
Enter the pairing code for EQO
Open the pairing-code dialog. Reply with the code, or code and pairing port (optionally connection port), separated by spaces.
Use six-digit code, pairing port, then optional connection port, separated by spaces or commas. Ports must be 1024–65535 and different. Connect to Wi-Fi first.
Code accepted for up to one minute. Keep the pairing dialog open while EQO finds the connection port, or reply again with code, pairing port and connection port. Pairing has not started yet.
Paired securely. Return to EQO and tap Connect again to start the helper and approve its prompt.
Could not pair securely. Reopen the pairing dialog and try its new code. Return to EQO if ports need to be entered.
Enter the connection port (the IP address and port value on the Wireless debugging screen).
Pairing forgotten. Pair again to connect.
Not checked — an earlier step did not pass.

resources.string: Start with setup, then type a task. EQO makes a plan for you to approve before it runs. You can use contact names, phone numbers or emails. Messaging steps can press Send; review the recipient and every step.
Tap to enter or check your provider key.
Tap to open Android settings and turn on screen control.
Tap to pair through Android\'s Wireless debugging screen and connect.
Tap to open the wireless debugging steps. The helper must report its own healthy connection.
Tap to choose whether browser control may be used. It is optional and unavailable in this build.
Ready. Tap to review or change this item.
Checking — wait for the result before checking again.
Unavailable in this build. You cannot finish this item here; tap for details.
Enter both the API key and model name, then tap Check and save key.
The key could not be saved securely. Check your phone storage and try Check and save key again.
OpenRouter rejected the key. Copy the whole key again, then check it.
OpenRouter is busy. Wait a while, then tap Check and save key. EQO will not retry automatically.
Your OpenRouter account needs credit. Add credit at openrouter.ai/credits, then check again.
This model cannot handle the request. Choose another model name from OpenRouter, then check again.
Could not reach OpenRouter. Check your internet connection, then check again. EQO will not retry automatically.
1. Open Android Settings → Accessibility → Downloaded apps (the name may vary by phone).\n2. Select EQO and turn it on after reading Android’s warning.\n3. Come back here to see the check result.
Check complete. Screen control status updated.
Next: choose whether to allow browser control. No choice has been saved yet.
Not started. Type a request, then tap Plan.
Type a request and review the whole plan. Nothing runs until you approve. Pause waits for the current step; Stop ends the run; Take over returns control to you.
Open an SMS draft (does not send)
Paused — resume only when you choose and confirm.
Completed — check the result on your phone.
The helper stopped responding. Return to setup to review its connection.

Draft opened in the messaging app. Nothing was sent.
This step did not run. It was skipped or cancelled before completion; check the task result above.

EQO asks permission to read Contacts only when a plan uses a name. You can type phone numbers and emails too. The preview shows the resolved recipient before you approve. Messaging steps may press Send in the open app. Review every step before approving.
Making a plan — nothing is running yet.

Optional EQO shortcuts on other screens; requires EQO Accessibility. Tap or swipe inward to open. Opening the panel pauses an active run after its current action finishes. Closing it does not resume: use the task screen to confirm Resume. Drag vertically to move, or across the screen to switch edge. Long press for Hide for this app. The keyboard or full-screen videos and games may hide the handle. It never reads or sends the screen. Unavailable shortcuts are omitted from the panel; your choices are kept.
